'''Ōhesoki no Mikoto''' (大綜麻杵命, birth and death dates unknown) was an ancient Japanese aristocrat and the ancestor of the {{ill|Mononobe clan|en|Mononobe clan|qid=Q1755836|lt=Mononobe no Muraji}}. He is also referred to as Ōsoki no Mikoto in the {{ill|Kujiki|en|Kujiki|qid=Q2716751|lt=Sendai Kuji Hongi}} and as Ōhesosoki no Mikoto in the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|Shinsen Shōjiroku|qid=Q1045362|lt=Shinsen Shōjiroku}}.

== Overview ==
In the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|qid=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}}, Ōhesoki is noted as the father of [[Ikashikome no Mikoto]], the mother of [[:en:Sujin Emperor|Sujin Emperor]]. While his other activities are not extensively recorded in the *Nihon Shoki*, the *Sendai Kuji Hongi*'s "Tenson Honki" section recounts that in the 8th year of Emperor Kōgen's reign, Ōhesoki was appointed as Ōne, a high-Ranking ministerial position, and his brother [[Utsushikome no Mikoto]] became Ōomi (Minister). He later became Ōomi under Emperor Kaika in the 8th year of his reign.

In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|Shinsen Shōjiroku|qid=Q1045362|lt=Shinsen Shōjiroku}}, he is identified as the grandfather of Tatetsukawa no Mikoto, indicating his importance in early genealogy.

Although the early genealogy of the Mononobe clan is somewhat inconsistent across historical sources, there is a general agreement that Ōhesoki was a fifth-generation descendant of {{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|饒速日命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nigihayahi no Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to QID FIXED|qid=Q10949054|lt=Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q10949054}} and a sibling to [[Utsushikome no Mikoto]]<ref>{{Cite book|author=Hoga Toshio|title=Research on Ancient Clans Vol. 8: The Mononobe Clan|publisher=Aogaki Publishing|year=2016|page=104|chapter=Four: Early Movements of the Mononobe Clan}}</ref>.
